scenario: A global health agency selects logistics officers who demonstrate epidemiological modelling competence OR advanced supply-chain optimisation skill. The competencies are independent in the applicant pool; OR-gate selection induces a negative within-officer correlation.

data.description: Population base rates and OR-gate selection mechanism

values.selection_rule: OR gate: selected if (epidemiological modelling competence) OR (supply-chain optimisation skill)

question: (a) Derive P(selected) from the OR-gate model. (b) Compute P(epi_modelling | ¬supply_chain, selected) and explain why it equals 1. (c) Compute P(epi_modelling | supply_chain, selected) and show it equals P(epi_modelling). (d) Quantify the induced conditional correlation direction and explain why it is a selection artefact rather than a genuine population relationship between epidemiological modelling competence and supply-chain optimisation skill.

ground_truth.explanation: Under OR-gate selection a candidate who lacks supply-chain optimisation skill must possess epidemiological modelling competence to be admitted — hence P(epi_modelling|¬supply_chain,sel)=1.0. A candidate who already has supply-chain optimisation skill is admitted regardless of epidemiological modelling competence, so P(epi_modelling|supply_chain,sel)=P(epi_modelling)=0.37. The gap (1.0 vs 0.37) creates a negative within-selected correlation that is purely a collider-selection artefact.

naive_answer: The negative correlation between epidemiological modelling competence and supply-chain optimisation skill observed among selected candidates reflects a genuine trade-off between these traits in the domain.
naive_trap: The negative correlation is entirely a Berkson collider artefact produced by the OR-gate admission rule; the two traits are independent in the full population.
reasoning_trace: (1) P(sel)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A)P(B)=0.37+0.47-0.37×0.47=0.6661. (2) Among candidates without supply-chain optimisation skill: only those with epidemiological modelling competence are selected → P(epi_modelling|¬supply_chain,sel)=1.0. (3) Among candidates with supply-chain optimisation skill: selected regardless of epidemiological modelling competence → P(epi_modelling|supply_chain,sel)=P(epi_modelling)=0.37. (4) Within-selected: knowing ¬supply_chain raises P(epi_modelling) from 0.37 to 1.0 → negative conditional correlation despite population independence.
python_verification:
pA,pB = 0.37,0.47
pSel = pA+pB-pA*pB
assert abs(pSel-0.6661)<0.005, f'pSel={pSel}'
pA_notB_sel = pA*(1-pB)/(pA*(1-pB))   # =1.0 by definition
assert abs(pA_notB_sel-1.0)<1e-9
pA_B_sel = pA*pB/pB                    # =pA by definition
assert abs(pA_B_sel-0.37)<1e-9
assert pA_notB_sel > pA_B_sel, 'negative collider correlation confirmed'
